paper_title: Do direct detection experiments constrain axionlike particles coupled to electrons?
suggested_experiment_name: X-ray and gamma-ray limits on ALP-electron coupling (NuSTAR/XMM/INTEGRAL)
notes: This is a phenomenology/reinterpretation paper, not a new experimental measurement. It argues that keV-MeV ALPs coupled to electrons decay too quickly to be dark matter, undermining existing direct detection limits (GERDA, EDELWEISS-III, SuperCDMS, Majorana) and noting X-ray/gamma-ray astronomy constraints. While it concerns g_ae (AxionElectron coupling), the paper presents no new tabulated numerical exclusion data — Fig. 2 reproduces existing limits and overlays lifetime/astrophysical regions. No extractable (mass, coupling) data points are provided in text or tables. | Vision: Figure 2. The lower constraint boundary is set by the X-ray/gamma-ray (light grey) region which supersedes direct detection limits for m_a > 6 keV. At lowest masses (<6 keV) the boundary follows direct detection sensitivity ~1e-13. The X-ray/gamma-ray limit descends steeply with mass. X-axis in MeV converted to eV. Values approximate due to jagged curve. | Calibration: No calibration needed
